portName: Port of Venice (Marittima, San Basilio, Porto Marghera and Fusina)
seoTitle: Venice cruise port 2026: Marghera, Fusina or Marittima?
seoDescription: Venice cruise port 2026: ships over 25,000 GT berth at Marghera or Fusina, not Marittima. Vaporetto €9.50, St Mark's Basilica €10, Doge's Palace €35.
quickAnswer: Only ships up to 25,000 GT still berth in the city, at Marittima or San Basilio; larger ships use Porto Marghera or Fusina on the mainland, and some 'Venice' cruises sail from Trieste, Monfalcone or Ravenna. From Marittima, take the People Mover or walk to Piazzale Roma, then a vaporetto to San Marco: €9.50 for a 75-minute ticket (2026). From Marghera or Fusina, use the cruise line's transfer and be back at its pick-up point at least two hours before all-aboard.
intro: 'Venice' on a cruise ticket no longer means sailing past St Mark's. Since the 2021 decree, ships over 25,000 GT cannot use the Giudecca Canal, so the port runs a split system: small luxury and expedition ships at Marittima and San Basilio, everything else at the Liguria and Lombardia quays in Porto Marghera or at the Fusina terminal on the mainland. Some lines skip the lagoon entirely and sell Trieste, Monfalcone or Ravenna as Venice. More than 95% of calls in 2026 are embarkation or disembarkation days, so most passengers here are fitting the city around a flight or a check-in time. Work out your berth first; everything else follows from it.

terminals.name: Stazione Marittima (Santa Marta)
terminals.notes: Ships up to 25,000 GT only in 2026, mainly luxury and expedition ships. Also used by cruise lines as a check-in and transfer point for ships berthed at Marghera. The People Mover links it to Piazzale Roma and Tronchetto.

terminals.name: San Basilio
terminals.notes: Quay on the Zattere side of Dorsoduro, inside the city, for the smallest ships (also under the 25,000 GT limit). Walkable to the centre.

terminals.name: Porto Marghera (Liguria and Lombardia quays)
terminals.notes: Industrial port on the mainland, used by mid-size ships. Cruise lines run shuttle buses to Marittima or Piazzale Roma, about 15–20 minutes plus queuing. Not walkable.

terminals.name: Fusina
terminals.notes: Mainland terminal south of Marghera with two quays, fully operational since August 2024. Opened the 2026 season with Viking Star on 16 March. Use the transfer your cruise line arranges.

terminals.name: Chioggia
terminals.notes: Fishing town at the southern end of the lagoon. 23 cruise calls by 9 ships in 2026. About an hour or more from Venice by road or boat.

terminals.name: Trieste, Monfalcone, Ravenna (sold as 'Venice')
terminals.notes: Figure is for Trieste, about 165 km away (just over 2 hours by fast train). Monfalcone is about 1.5 hours away; Ravenna (Porto Corsini) about 2.5 hours by road. These are separate ports, not Venice.

walkability.detail: From Marittima you can walk to Piazzale Roma and on through the city to St Mark's in about 30–45 minutes, crossing many stepped bridges. From San Basilio the centre is also walkable. From Porto Marghera, Fusina, Chioggia or the ports outside the lagoon, walking into Venice is not possible.

transportSections.cost: €1.50 one way (2026); also valid with ACTV 75-minute tickets and day passes
transportSections.detail: Elevated shuttle train every few minutes from early morning to late evening. From Marittima it takes you to Piazzale Roma, where the vaporetto lines start. Cruise lines berthed at Marghera often drop passengers at Marittima or Piazzale Roma too.

transportSections.cost: €9.50 for a 75-minute ticket; €25 for 24 hours, €35 for 48 hours, €45 for 72 hours (2026)
transportSections.time: Allow 45–60 minutes from the gangway at Marittima to St Mark's
transportSections.detail: From Piazzale Roma, line 1 calls at every stop along the Grand Canal to San Marco and is the slowest; line 2 makes fewer stops. Buy tickets from machines or ticket offices before boarding: cash is not accepted on board. Passes do not cover Alilaguna boats, the airport ACTV service or lines 16, 19 and 21.

transportSections.time: Marghera to Marittima about 15–20 minutes plus queuing
transportSections.detail: From Marghera, plan 75–90 minutes each way between the ship and St Mark's. Check in the daily programme where the shuttle drops off, when the last one leaves and whether it is free. From Fusina, use the line's boat or coach transfer.

transportSections.cost: Not covered by ACTV tickets; check fares with the operator
transportSections.detail: Private boat company running the Blu, Arancio, Rossa and Verde lines, mainly between the airport and the city. Stops include San Marco, San Zaccaria, Zattere, Rialto and Lido. Useful on embarkation or disembarkation day; stops are sometimes moved for regattas and events.

transportSections.cost: Expensive; agree the price before boarding
transportSections.detail: Licensed water taxis carry several people and luggage. Worth it for limited mobility or a tight flight connection, not for a single traveller on a budget.
Only practical from Marittima and San Basilio. Expect bridges with steps, narrow lanes and crowds.

returnTiming.rule: From Marittima or San Basilio, leave St Mark's 2 hours before all-aboard. From Marghera or Fusina, be at the cruise line's pick-up point at least 2 hours before all-aboard (15:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard).
returnTiming.detail: The trip from St Mark's to Marittima takes 45–60 minutes by vaporetto and People Mover, and vaporetti fill up in the afternoon. From Marghera, add the shuttle time and the queue for it. Ships at Trieste, Monfalcone or Ravenna are 1.5 to 2.5 hours from Venice each way, which leaves little time in the city.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If you miss the last shuttle, a taxi from Piazzale Roma reaches the mainland quays by road. Call the port agent number in your daily programme as soon as you know you will be late. Ships do not wait.

diyVsExcursion.diy: €9.50 vaporetto each way from Piazzale Roma (2026), plus €1.50 People Mover from Marittima

excursionAdvice: If your ship is at Marittima or San Basilio, Venice needs no excursion. At Marghera or Fusina, the line's shuttle does most of the work, and a guided tour mainly saves you the vaporetto and the queues. If your 'Venice' call is really Trieste, Monfalcone or Ravenna, the ship's coach to Venice is the safer option: the round trip eats 3 to 5 hours, and the ship will wait for its own coach but not for you. In that case, spending the day in the port city itself is often the better choice.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes a transit call docking at 08:00 at Marghera with a cruise line shuttle to Marittima, and pre-booked timed tickets for the Basilica and Doge's Palace.

steps.what: Shuttle from the ship to Marittima, then the People Mover to Piazzale Roma.
Vaporetto line 1 down the Grand Canal to San Marco on a 75-minute ticket.
St Mark's Basilica with a timed ticket. Leave bags at the deposit first; shoulders and knees covered.
Doge's Palace on a timed slot, including the Bridge of Sighs route. About 1.5–2 hours.
Walk to Rialto (about 15 minutes) for cicchetti at a bacaro near the market.
Rialto Bridge, then vaporetto from Rialto back to Piazzale Roma.
People Mover to Marittima and the shuttle back to the ship.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: St Mark's Basilica
sights.why: The gold-mosaic church at the heart of Venice.
sights.cost: €10 basic; €20 with the Pala d'Oro or with the Museum and Horses Loggia; €30 full ticket (2026); free under 11
sights.tip: Book a timed slot on the official site, tickets.basilicasanmarco.it. No bags are allowed inside; use the free deposit nearby. On Sunday mornings only the Museum and Horses Loggia ticket is sold.

sights.name: Doge's Palace
sights.why: Seat of the Venetian Republic, with the council halls, prisons and Bridge of Sighs.
sights.cost: €35, or €30 online 30+ days ahead; reduced €15 (2026). Includes Museo Correr, the National Archaeological Museum and the Marciana Library rooms
sights.tip: Open 09:00–19:00 April to October (last entry 18:00) and 09:00–18:00 November to March. Tickets without a timed slot only admit you from 12:00, so book a slot for a morning visit.

sights.name: St Mark's Campanile
sights.why: The bell tower over the square, with a lift to the top for views of the lagoon.
sights.tip: Sold by the Basilica's ticket office; free-entry categories do not apply.

sights.name: Grand Canal by vaporetto
sights.why: The cheapest way to see the palaces along the canal.
sights.tip: Line 1 stops everywhere and moves slowly, which is the point. Sit at the front or back for open views.

sights.name: Rialto Bridge and market
sights.why: The oldest bridge over the Grand Canal and the produce and fish market next to it.
sights.tip: The market is a morning affair; go before lunch.

sights.name: Murano and Burano
sights.why: Glass-making island and the island of painted houses.
sights.cost: €9.50 each way, or covered by a day pass (2026)
sights.tip: Only realistic on a long call or an overnight. Burano is the farther of the two.

sights.name: Museo Correr
sights.why: City museum on the square, included in the Doge's Palace ticket.
sights.cost: Included with the St Mark's Square Museums ticket (2026)
sights.tip: A good indoor stop if it rains.

beaches.name: Lido di Venezia
beaches.howToGetThere: Vaporetto from San Zaccaria or Piazzale Roma to Lido S.M.E., then walk across the island to the beach.
beaches.time: Allow an hour each way from Marittima
beaches.cost: €9.50 each way, or a day pass (2026)
beaches.note: Long sandy beach on the Adriatic side. Much of it is run by private beach concessions; public stretches exist. The Lido is outside the access-fee zone.

food.dish: Cicchetti and a glass of wine
food.where: Cantina Do Mori, near the Rialto market

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming 'Venice' means the ship docks in the city.
commonMistakes.fix: Check the exact berth in your booking documents and daily programme: Marittima, San Basilio, Marghera, Fusina, Chioggia, or a port outside the lagoon such as Trieste, Monfalcone or Ravenna.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to pay for the vaporetto on board in cash.
commonMistakes.fix: Buy a 75-minute ticket or a day pass from a machine or ticket office before boarding.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at the Basilica with a backpack or handbag.
commonMistakes.fix: No bags are allowed inside. Use the deposit or travel light.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying a Doge's Palace ticket without a time slot for a morning visit.
commonMistakes.fix: Untimed tickets admit you only from 12:00. Book a timed slot, and book 30 days ahead for the €30 online price.

commonMistakes.mistake: Underestimating the return from St Mark's to a mainland quay.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow at least two hours from St Mark's to the ship at Marghera or Fusina, including the shuttle queue.

commonMistakes.mistake: Ignoring the access fee on a fee day.
commonMistakes.fix: If a future season repeats the scheme, check the calendar on the city's official site and pay online before your call date.

safety: Venice is safe for daytime visitors. The main risks are pickpockets on crowded vaporetti, at the Rialto and around St Mark's, and slips on wet stone and bridge steps. Keep bags closed and in front on the water buses. In late autumn and winter, acqua alta (high water) can flood St Mark's Square and low-lying lanes; follow the raised walkways and the city's tide alerts.
scams: Unofficial resellers selling St Mark's Basilica entry at a mark-up. The Basilica's own site, tickets.basilicasanmarco.it, is the only official ticket office; basic entry is €10 (2026).
Water taxi drivers quoting high fares to cruise passengers at Piazzale Roma and Tronchetto. Use licensed taxis and agree the price before you board.
Restaurant bills near St Mark's with cover and service charges you did not expect. Check the menu for 'coperto' and 'servizio' before you sit down.
accessibility: Venice has more than 400 bridges, most with steps, so step-free routes are limited. Vaporetti are the best option for wheelchair users: most stops are floating pontoons and the boats take wheelchairs. The People Mover links Marittima to Piazzale Roma without steps. People with disabilities and one companion enter St Mark's Basilica free. At Marghera and Fusina, ask the cruise line for an adapted shuttle in advance.
rainyDay: The Doge's Palace and the museums on the St Mark's Square ticket (Museo Correr, the National Archaeological Museum and the Marciana Library rooms) fill a wet morning under one €35 ticket (2026). The Basilica is indoors but has a queue outside. A ride on vaporetto line 1 lets you see the Grand Canal from under cover.
crowdTips: St Mark's Square, the Rialto and the lanes between them are busiest from late morning to mid-afternoon. In 2026 the city charged a day-tripper access fee on 60 days between 3 April and 26 July, from 08:30 to 16:00: €5 booked at least four days ahead, €10 after that, under-14s exempt. There was no general exemption for cruise passengers; time spent only at Marittima, San Basilio, Piazzale Roma, Tronchetto or the station was not charged. The 2026 trial ended on 26 July, and the city must approve any scheme for later years.

faqs.q: Where do cruise ships dock in Venice in 2026?
faqs.a: Ships up to 25,000 GT berth at Marittima or San Basilio in the city. Larger ships use the Liguria and Lombardia quays at Porto Marghera or the Fusina terminal on the mainland, and a few call at Chioggia. Some 'Venice' cruises actually sail from Trieste, Monfalcone or Ravenna.

faqs.q: How do I know which Venice port my ship uses?
faqs.a: Look for the berth name in your booking documents, boarding pass or daily programme, or ask the cruise line. If it says Trieste, Monfalcone or Ravenna, you are 1.5 to 2.5 hours from Venice.

faqs.q: How do I get from the Venice cruise port to St Mark's Square?
faqs.a: From Marittima, take the People Mover (€1.50) or walk to Piazzale Roma, then vaporetto line 1 or 2 to San Marco on a €9.50 75-minute ticket (2026). From Marghera or Fusina, take the cruise line's transfer first.
Only from Marittima and San Basilio. St Mark's is 30–45 minutes on foot from Marittima. Marghera and Fusina are on the mainland and not walkable.

faqs.q: Do cruise passengers pay the Venice access fee?
faqs.a: In 2026 there was no general exemption for cruise passengers entering the historic centre on fee days (60 days between 3 April and 26 July, 08:30–16:00). Staying in the terminal areas, Piazzale Roma or Tronchetto was not charged. The 2026 trial is over; check the city's site for any future dates.

faqs.q: How much are St Mark's Basilica and Doge's Palace tickets?
faqs.a: The Basilica is €10 basic or €30 with the Pala d'Oro, Museum and Horses Loggia. The Doge's Palace is €35, or €30 if bought online at least 30 days ahead (2026).

faqs.q: What can I do in Venice in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Take the vaporetto down the Grand Canal, visit St Mark's Basilica and the Doge's Palace on timed tickets, have cicchetti at Rialto, and head back early. Murano and Burano only fit on a long call.

faqs.q: Is Venice safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes. Watch for pickpockets on crowded water buses and around Rialto and St Mark's, and take care on wet bridge steps.
